newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Hilasal sees 1998 output surging.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Hilasal sees 1998 output surging.

text.p: Mexico's Hilasal S.A. expects output in 1998 to be nearly three times greater than its production before the peso devaluation of 1994, the textile manufacturer's director general told Reuters on Monday.
"We will triple production in 1998. ...(The forecast) is not a target but based on contracts -- it is a fact," Hilasal Director General Jorge Garcia Fernandez said.
"In 1994 we produced 220,000 meters, and I believe we will easily surpass 600,000 meters," in 1998, Garcia added.

Hilasal floated 27.71 percent of its shareholding equity on the Mexican stock market in June 1996. The company posted full-year revenues of 153.14 million pesos for 1996 and net earnings of 32.73 million pesos.
